why: Reviewers found P18 units are writing rules (editing, translation, drafting), not a prose-versus-code distinction.

options.name: AI for editing, proofreading and outlining one's own work
options.covers: AI may help with editing, proofreading, grammar, outlining, organizing or revising one's own writing. P18 is about treating prose differently from code; this is the permission itself. Evidence: Morehouse, Rutgers, NAU, Ohio State, Oakland, Rowan, Penn State, Rush, NC State.

options.name: AI-generated content or code in submitted work
options.covers: Students may submit or use AI-generated code under explicit conditions (small snippets, line or percentage caps, cited, specific projects, or freely).

options.name: AI for translation and language support
options.covers: Rules on using AI to translate text or to support language learning (permitted, conditioned or banned). Split out of P18 and from reviewer NEW labels.

options.name: Routine or minor AI uses outside the rules
options.covers: Routine embedded features (spell-check, grammar check, search, autocomplete) are allowed or need no disclosure even under a restrictive rule. Evidence: Oregon State, Morehouse, Pepperdine.

options.name: AI feedback or critique on one's own work
options.covers: Using AI to get feedback, critique or review of one's own draft, code or solution (not to produce it). From P14, P91 subgroups and NEW labels.

options.name: AI for brainstorming and early planning
options.covers: AI may be used for brainstorming, idea generation, or exploring alternative approaches.

units.passage: Sample Statements for Teachers Prohibiting the Use of Generative AI: Generative AI Use Is Prohibited The use of generative AI is strictly prohibited in this course. Closed Book Exam/Quiz The use of AI tools is not permitted. General Writing The use of generative AI tools is not permitted on writing assignments in this course. By submitting a writing assignment, you attest that you are the only and original author. Computer Code The use of generative AI tools to develop code is strictly prohibited in this course.
units.why: Sample writing statement: AI tools 'not permitted on writing assignments'. A prose-specific rule separate from code (P18).

units.passage: You may not use generative AI to do ANY writing whatsoever, including the earliest of rough drafts or the latest of copy edits.
units.policy: You may not use generative AI to do ANY writing whatsoever, including the earliest of rough drafts or the latest of copy edits.
units.why: Bars generative AI for 'ANY writing whatsoever', from rough drafts to copy edits: a prose-specific ban (P18) on AI-produced and edited writing.

units.passage: Documentation: AI-generated text may be used for code comments, explanations, and other documentation, as long as it is properly cited.
units.why: "AI-generated text may be used for code comments, explanations, and other documentation, as long as it is properly cited" permits AI prose for documentation with citation; the prose/code split, P18.

units.passage: Guided use of GAI is encouraged as the best approach to further, rather than undermine, learning outcomes.
units.why: For writing courses the report says 'Guided use of GAI is encouraged as the best approach to further, rather than undermine, learning outcomes.' It treats prose separately from code and encourages guided use, so P18.

units.passage: All comments should be your own words.
units.why: "All comments should be your own words" sets a prose rule for code comments, separate from the code rules (P18); the source says 'should', so should.
